card.title: 4th BRIGADE NZ
card.text: Deployment: If you have less than 3 cards in hand, draw until you have 3.
card.flavorText: The 4th Infantry Brigade served as part of the 2nd New Zealand Division, New Zealand’s main expeditionary formation during WWII. Re-raised in 1939, the brigade consisted of the 18th, 19th and 20th Battalions and was one of the division’s three infantry brigades. Its first major campaign with the division came in Greece in 1941. The 2nd New Zealand Division fought alongside the Australian 6th Division against the German invasion, with the 4th Brigade defending the Aliakmon Line and later Servia Pass, before withdrawing to Thermopylae. The brigade was then evacuated to Crete, where it served as a reserve formation around Galatas. Later, the brigade rejoined the 2nd New Zealand Division in North Africa. In July 1942, it attacked Ruweisat Ridge, where a German counterattack inflicted severe losses on the 19th and 20th Battalions. The brigade was rebuilt soon afterwards and, in October 1942, converted into the 4th New Zealand Armoured Brigade, continuing to serve within the 2nd New Zealand Division.
